messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

So includes melting at 0°C, heating liquid water to 100°C, then boiling at 100°C? Actually final state is 100°C, but not specified whether it's still solid or liquid. Under 1 atm, water at 100°C is saturated vapor. But if we heat ice to 100°C, it will melt, then boil. So final state is water vapor at 100°C. So we need total entropy change: ΔS = ΔS_melt + ΔS_heat_liquid + ΔS_vaporization.

But we can compute using known values: latent heat of fusion L_f = 334 kJ/kg, latent heat of vaporization L_v = 2260 kJ/kg (approx). Specific heat capacities: c_ice ~ 2.09 kJ/(kg·K), c_water ~ 4.18 kJ/(kg·K). For water vapor, cp ~ 1.86 kJ/(kg·K) but we don't need because final state is vapor at 100°C; we might need to account for heating vapor from 0°C? Wait we start at 0°C ice. We melt at 0°C, so no temperature change during phase change. Then heat liquid water from 0°C to 100°C. Then vaporize at 100°C. So we don't need to heat vapor further. So ΔS_total = ΔS_melt + ΔS_heat_liquid + ΔS_vaporization.

Entropy change for melting: ΔS_fusion = L_f / T_melt (T=273.15 K). For heating liquid: ΔS_heat_liquid = ∫ c_water dT / T from 273.15 to 373.15 K. Since c_water constant, integral = c_water ln(T_final/T_initial). For vaporization: ΔS_vaporization = L_v / T_boiling (T=373.15 K).

Compute numeric:

L_f = 334 kJ/kg = 334000 J/kg. T_melt = 273.15 K. So ΔS_fusion = 334000/273.15 ≈ 1223.5 J/K.

c_water = 4180 J/(kg·K). Ln(373.15/273.15) = ln(1.366) ≈ 0.312. Multiply: 4180*0.312 ≈ 1305 J/K.

L_v = 2260 kJ/kg = 2260000 J/kg. T_boiling = 373.15 K. ΔS_vaporization = 2260000/373.15 ≈ 6057 J/K.

Total ΔS = 1223.5 + 1305 + 6057 ≈ 8585.5 J/K.
